response.markdown_report:
The best first experiment is **terminal-aligned mixed masking within the supplied BERT4Rec**, using one network per category. It targets training–inference alignment while preserving the corrected backbone and evaluation protocol. No improvement is established before validation.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, appended-mask inference predicts from a prefix; interior reconstruction can exploit later interactions, creating a different learning problem. Second, users report both stale interests and broad matches displacing specific choices, motivating supervision on actual next choices. Third, Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%, identifying weak separation as a measurable concern. Fourth, embedding scores near 0.5 imply mean cosine similarity near zero; they do not justify collapse remedies.

**Insights from related work.** Original [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes terminal masking, so this proposal refines its sampling rather than inventing that objective. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates closer alignment between masking and sequential prediction, without proving gains here. [Sampled Softmax](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) highlights objective and temperature sensitivity, supporting a separate controlled objective experiment. [Semantic Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) motivates contextual content integration, but semantic resemblance cannot establish equipment compatibility.

The resulting framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Diagnostic target | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prediction alignment | Prefix-terminal masking | Current priorities; weak margins | Best sampling proportion |
| Candidate discrimination | Uniform sampled softmax | Broad matches; wrong ranks | Unobserved false negatives |
| Content specificity | Joint title/description gate | Fine distinctions | Sparse text and compatibility ambiguity |

Three candidate ideas are assessed below. Scores are hypotheses, not measured outcomes; difficulty 10 means hardest. Each entry gives its principal benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed prefix-terminal masking | 3: grounded / established | 7: reusable / limited novelty | 7: recent choices / intent latent | 7: aligned separation / gain uncertain | 2: sampler change / leakage checks |
| Uniform sampled softmax | 3: established / little novelty | 7: scalable / tuning sensitive | 5: discrimination / weak specificity | 8: direct separation / false negatives | 4: shared candidates / exclusions |
| Gated text–ID embeddings | 5: useful combination / precedented | 7: richer inputs / sparse metadata | 8: finer distinctions / no ownership evidence | 6: richer features / benefit uncertain | 6: joint encoder / predictor changes |

Select mixed prefix-terminal masking at 0% research progress. Use terminal examples for half the training examples and retain corrected interior masking for the remainder. Sample a training prefix, remove its target and every later interaction, then append the reserved mask. Preserve the baseline loss initially to isolate sampling.

This explicitly targets two user failures: stale historical emphasis and broad relevance displacing specific next choices. It also targets weak positive–negative separation, without claiming to infer compatibility. Compare against the supplied baseline using macro validation HR@10; margin diagnostics remain secondary. Unknown-item skips remain unassessable feedback.

idea.description: Replace half of corrected BERT4Rec training examples with randomly sampled prefix-terminal masked examples, retaining one shared bidirectional Transformer and the baseline loss. The terminal target and every subsequent interaction are excluded from that example's input.
idea.motivation: Terminal examples match appended-mask inference and emphasize observed next choices. This addresses stale-interest emphasis and insufficient distinction between broadly relevant items and specific next choices, while testing whether the weaker margin tails in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics improve. These are hypotheses; neither compatibility nor present intent is directly observed.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep the supplied training, data routing, checkpoint selection and predictor writer. Change only family-specific example sampling initially; no architecture or inference change is required. Apply the example-type mixture per example, with probability 0.5 for terminal masking. Retain the corrected baseline's interior-mask branch and loss unchanged. Use only each user's training history. Seed preprocessing with 0 and training with 42; keep at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and trial-local artifacts. Train and load exactly one checkpoint per category. Preserve ModelView.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. DiagnosisProbe must score only supervised masked positions; it must not score visible targets or interpret unavailable categories. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and definitions. The helper below returns an example, its aligned positive labels, and its supervision mask; connect these to the supplied sample_batch and existing loss rather than replacing the host pipeline. The available prompt contains no baseline source, so this is an integration helper, not a standalone train.py replacement.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np


def terminal_masked_example(history, maxlen, mask_id, rng):
    """history contains only real training-item IDs; rng is seeded by caller."""
    if maxlen < 2 or len(history) < 2:
        raise ValueError('Need room for context and a mask, and two interactions')
    # t is the target index. Neither history[t] nor any later item is input.
    t = int(rng.integers(1, len(history)))
    context = np.asarray(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t], dtype=np.int64)
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    positive = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    sequence[-len(context)-1:-1] = context
    sequence[-1] = mask_id
    positive[-1] = int(history[t])
    supervised = positive != 0
    return sequence, positive, supervised

originality.positive: A controlled prefix-sampling refinement directly connects the observed failure patterns to inference-aligned supervision.
originality.negative: Terminal masking is already part of original BERT4Rec; the contribution is experimental design and sampling emphasis.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost experiment can establish whether objective alignment deserves further work before adding content or mining.
future_potential.negative: It cannot resolve missing compatibility evidence, and stronger training margins may not improve validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: The change is confined primarily to example construction and preserves architecture and checkpoint formats.
code_difficulty.negative: Target exclusion, truncation, supervised-position diagnostics and left-padding readout require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Includes terminal masking and appended-mask next-item inference.
limitations: Does not establish the best prefix-terminal sampling proportion for this benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling
contributions: Motivates sampling objectives better aligned with sequential recommendation and recency.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed mixture on the four supplied datasets under the pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: Sampled Softmax for Item Recommendation
contributions: Studies efficient shared negative sampling and the influence of temperature.
limitations: Its findings do not establish improvements for this corrected BERT4Rec setup.
Unobserved sampled items may be false negatives.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion
contributions: Motivates contextual integration of semantic and item-ID representations.
limitations: Does not establish that a randomly initialized lightweight text encoder improves this benchmark.
Semantic similarity alone cannot establish compatibility or equipment ownership.
